chapter: New Orleans Rhythm Kings and Tin Roof Blues
title: Abbie's patched trombone, barbershop harmony and his view of the blues
summary: Brothers' band harmony at Abby's house, and his theory that blues came from Jewish hymns plus African rhythm.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: What the blues is, and why every jazz player needs it

blocks.x: There was a guy come in the club about two weeks ago, his name was Alexandra. He says, your brothers have got a pretty good band. He says, they played for our convention down in Bilox at the Buena Vista. He says, they got a pretty good band for a bunch of guys. He says, but tell me, how does your brother get music out of that patched up trombone he's got? Yeah, it's all patched up with tape. I'm going to buy him one and send him one. He likes it, he's used to it. Did you ever play a valve trombone? Did you ever try a valve trombone? Oh yeah, I can play that. Did you ever play a card? I got a tape, I got a tape, he was used to it.
Did you ever play a valve trombone?
Oh yeah, I can play that. Did you ever play card?
I got a tape, I got a tape that we took last New Year's.
Of course we were all blind at Abby's house, you know. And we were trying to play three way of harmony with the trombone and two trombones or two trumpets and trombone.
They do a lot of that on the job. Yeah, that's what they like.

They specialize in that harmony, that's pretty stuff. Of course it's barbershop, a lot of these progressive guys that call it corn and inky, but that's what started music. To me, blues comes from the Jewish hymn, like Ailey Ailey. Yeah. Then they took the African bongos or tom-tom and they made rhythm to it. That's my opinion of blues. The blues.
And to me all blues sound alike.
